points.description: The answer conveys that a data member belongs to the class and can be accessed from any member function of that class. Equivalent wording, such as 'available to all methods in the class', earns the mark.

The answer conveys that a local variable exists only within the member function that declares it and cannot be accessed outside that function. Equivalent wording, such as 'scope is limited to its function', earns the mark.

rubric.notes: Both points are needed for the difference, so the marks are split equally. Full marks require the scope of both kinds of variable to be stated correctly. Stating only one side, or describing the scopes incorrectly, earns no marks for the missing side. Alternative methods and wording are accepted.
